cards.b: A system of blood vessels with a pump (the heart) and valves to ensure one-way flow of blood.
Heart → gills → body → heart. Blood passes through the heart once per circuit, and pressure falls after the gills.
Blood passes through the heart twice per circuit: pulmonary (heart → lungs → heart) and systemic (heart → body → heart).
Blood reaches the body at high pressure (faster delivery of oxygen and glucose); lungs get lower pressure so capillaries are not damaged.

cards.f: Trace the flow of blood through the heart
cards.b: Vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta.

cards.f: What is the septum, and what do valves do?
cards.b: Septum: separates left and right sides so blood does not mix. Valves: one-way, prevent backflow.
Supply the heart muscle with oxygen and glucose.
Coronary arteries become blocked (fatty deposits, clot), so heart muscle gets less oxygen and glucose and may die.
Diet (saturated fat, salt), lack of exercise, stress, smoking, genetic predisposition, age, sex (more common in males).

cards.f: Three ways to monitor heart activity
cards.b: ECG (electrocardiogram), pulse rate, listening to the sounds of valves closing.

cards.f: Why does heart rate rise during exercise?
cards.b: Muscles respire faster and need more oxygen and glucose and produce more CO₂, so the heart beats faster to deliver and remove them.
Artery: thick wall, narrow lumen, high pressure. Vein: thin wall, wide lumen, valves. Capillary: one cell thick, very narrow, exchange.
Pulmonary artery: deoxygenated blood from heart to lungs. Pulmonary vein: oxygenated blood from lungs to heart.

cards.f: Functions of red cells, white cells, platelets and plasma
cards.b: Red: carry oxygen (haemoglobin). White: phagocytosis and antibodies. Platelets: clotting. Plasma: transports cells, ions, nutrients, urea, hormones, CO₂.
Phagocyte: engulfs pathogens (phagocytosis). Lymphocyte: produces antibodies.

short.q: Explain how the structure of an artery is related to the pressure of blood it carries. [3]
short.model: Arteries carry blood at high pressure, so they have thick, muscular and elastic walls to withstand it and a narrow lumen.
points: thick muscular / elastic wall withstands pressure

short.q: Explain how a capillary is adapted for exchange of substances. [3]
short.model: Its wall is one cell thick, giving a short diffusion distance; there are many capillaries giving a large surface area; narrow lumen slows blood for exchange.
points: wall one cell thick, short diffusion distance

short.q: Describe the pathway of blood from the lungs to the body, naming the heart chambers and vessels. [3]
short.model: Pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

short.q: Describe how diet and exercise can reduce the risk of coronary heart disease. [3]
short.model: Eating less saturated fat and salt means fewer fatty deposits in arteries; regular exercise strengthens the heart, controls body mass and lowers blood pressure.
points: fewer fatty deposits blocking coronary arteries
exercise strengthens heart / controls mass / lowers blood pressure

short.q: Explain why the heart rate increases during exercise. [3]
short.model: Muscles respire faster, needing more oxygen and glucose and producing more CO₂, so the heart beats faster to supply them and remove CO₂.
points: need more oxygen and glucose / produce more CO₂
heart beats faster to deliver and remove
